newsitem.title: USA: Deluxe to take Q4 restructuring charge.
newsitem.headline: Deluxe to take Q4 restructuring charge.

text.p: Deluxe Corp said Monday it will take a $140 million to $150 million pretax charge in the fourth quarter to complete a restructuring plan announced in December 1995.

A $40 million pretax gain on the sale of Deluxe's Colwell business unit in October will partially offset the charge. The company said it expects to achieve its publicly announced per-share earnings before adjustments target of $0.50 for the fourth quarter and $1.85 for the full year.

Deluxe said the charge is related to its recently announced decision to sell two businesses, PaperDirect Inc and the Social Expressions unit of Current Inc. It is writing off more than $110 million of goodwill incurred when it purchased these two units.

The writeoff reflects the difference between current book value on these two units and their likely sale value. Chairman J.A. Blanchard said the company retained Merrill Lynch to determine the market value of Current Social Expressions and PaperDirect.

"We will soon add Financial Processing Services to the list of divested businesses, which already includes T/Maker, Colwell, Internal Bank Forms and our Printwise ink division," Blanchard said in a statement, noting that Deluxe announced its intention to sell non-strategic businesses and to focus on increasing the value of its products and services to financial institutions.

In 1986, Deluxe closed 12 of the 26 plants it designated for consolidation. Additional closings scheduled in 1997 will move the company close to its stated target of 15 remaining check printing plants by 1998. The plan to reduce $150 milion in annual operating costs by 1998 remains on target, he added.
"This enhanced focus will strengthen our ability to deliver our previously stated 1997 earnings objective of at least $2.15 per share," Blanchard noted.
Deluxe, a printer of checks and bank forms, expects to release year-end financial results on January 21.
